boards.title: Needs review · a 22-note batch, grouped, with labels
Review · labels, folding groups, narrow window, History
boards.heading: Review: labels you can see, groups that fold
boards.intro: Review now scales to a big batch. Up top, one line says what changes (“22 new source pages · 3 new concepts · 1 new entity · 6 pages updated”). Below, three groups: New pages (entities and concepts, open), Updated (index, overview, log, hot cache, ledgers: named in its summary, opens for a note per page) and Sources: each source is listed once, merged with the source page it made and its labels. A group with more than 6 rows starts folded; folded Sources still shows the most used labels. Labels were suggested in the queue (3 files at a time) or by the batch, so they are already there. Approving confirms the labels shown (labels_by: user; they don’t come back in Labels → To review). Editing a source’s labels writes them into the change and the vault core checks it again before Approve comes back; if that check fails, the edit is not kept and nothing else changes. History uses the same layout (frame 8); the old hand-made History → Jobs board is superseded by it. When the batch’s AI session can’t be resumed any more, Distill says why and asks before starting a new one (frame 9).

boards.title: Review · pick sources, remove, approve without labels, several batches
boards.heading: Review: approve what you pick, remove what you don’t want
boards.intro: Sources can be picked one by one (all are picked at first). Approve adds the picked sources and confirms the labels shown; the menu next to it offers Approve, review labels later: the same pages with their labels unconfirmed, which then wait in Labels → To review. Remove (on hover) takes a source out of the batch: it is never added to the vault, its file stays in inbox/, and Undo puts it back while the batch is in Review. Approving only some sources needs a new change, because the index, log, hot cache, overview and ledgers cover the whole batch: the batch’s own Claude session rebuilds it for just those sources, the vault core checks it, and Distill compares it with what you approved (your source pages byte for byte, nothing from the other sources). The regenerated pages are text you have not seen, so you approve once more (frame 5). Sources you did not pick stay in Review in the same batch, with the same session. Several batches can wait at once: one tab each, oldest first, because the oldest was built against the oldest vault and should go in first; when another batch changed the vault first, the next one is rebuilt in its own session and says so. History lists each part that was applied.

boards.title: Review · after you approve: watch it go into your vault
boards.heading: Review after Approve: every step until it is in your vault
boards.intro: “Update the review, so I can see the progress after I approved: when the AI is starting the process, when all the approved files are added to my knowledgebase.” Today an approved batch leaves Review at once and nothing says what happens next. Now it stays, and one card shows the steps live: You approved, Claude starting (resuming this batch’s own session), applying through the vault core, Added with the counts from the checked plan, never from the AI (“22 source pages, 3 concepts, 1 entity added · 6 pages updated”), and the follow-up, finding actions. These are the batch’s live-log steps, so Show steps opens the full log. Approve and Reject go away while it runs; the sidebar count and the flask badge count only batches that need you. Once added, the card folds to one line, new pages open from their rows, Clean up inbox offers the batch’s files, and Done takes the batch out of Review (it is in History → Jobs). A failure says what happened and what to do, in the words Review already uses (frames E, F; more in ApplyProgress states). Part of a batch shows its own progress, and the sources left wait in the same batch (frame G).

sections.title: When something goes wrong, and parts of a batch

boards.title: Clean up inbox · move what is already in your knowledge base to the Trash
boards.heading: Clean up inbox: only what is safely in your knowledge base, only when you ask
boards.intro: “Let’s not do automatic for now, add a manual cleanup button.” claude-obsidian keeps inbox/ as yours: no operation writes it, and Distill never deletes from it on its own. Clean up is a button you press. A file can go only when the source ledger says it was added, the file has not changed since (same sha256), and every page made from it still exists. A note’s .distill.json goes with it, and a folder goes as one. Before anything moves you see what goes and what stays, and why: “not added yet”, “changed since it was added”, “its page is missing”, “waiting in Review”, “in the queue”. Files go to the macOS Trash, never deleted, and each is checked again when you press Move. Two places: a batch in History → Jobs (only that batch’s files; also on Review once a batch is added), and Settings → Batching for the whole vault, with select-all. Every clean-up is in Activity, with names and counts only.

sections.title: The whole vault, the rules, and the record
